Turning bad press into positive action

If you suffer from ME you probably won’t have failed to notice the horrendously inaccurate reporting of the UK press last Wednesday - claiming that CBT/GET is a cure for ME and that most sufferers were simply ‘thinking themselves ill’.

But on a bad day for ME it was incredibly heartening to see sufferers rally together to refute the reporting and broadcast the truth about this devastating illness. We’d like to say a big thank you to everyone who tweeted during wednesday’s #MEawarenesshour. It was clear from everyone’s tweets that there is an overwhelming amount of evidence that CBT/GET simply does not work and in many cases actually makes things worse.

In an interview @Sonyachowdury chief executive of @ActionforME said: ‘People are in dire situations and they cannot simply get better by thinking more positively and undertaking exercise.’

Dr Charles Shepherd echoed those words and backed them up with real evidence when he said in an interview: ‘We have a new report from the @MEassociation which has just come out that looked at patient experiences from over 1000 people about CBT and GET. It found around 70% thought CBT was ineffective and a similar number found GET made the condition worse.’

It’s only through getting our stories and personal experiences out there that we can combat the kind of misinformation reported in the press this week. That’s why initiatives like #MEawarenesshour are so important and why we can all make a difference - even if it’s from your sickbeds!

So thank you all so much and keep up the good work while remembering to pace yourselves.

We’d also like to say a special thank you to @AdloProject for supporting and helping us on Wednesday. We’re pleased to say that they are going to support us in the future too.

See you all next Wednesday!

Stephen Carroll @copysteve
